# tritonctl sandbox template

Templates: what a sandbox boots, and their builds

Subcommands: list, show, build, logs, delete, tag, untag

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl sandbox template list

List templates, the built-in ones included

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template list [OPTIONS]`

- `--builtin <BOOL>`: Only built-in templates (`true`), or only your own (`false`) (one of: true, false)

## tritonctl sandbox template show

Show one template and its builds

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template show [OPTIONS] <TEMPLATE>`

- `<TEMPLATE>`: Template name or uuid

## tritonctl sandbox template build

Start a build of a template, making the template if it is new.

Exits non-zero when the build fails, with the reason.

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template build [OPTIONS] <--image <REF>|--dockerfile <FILE>|--from-snapshot <SANDBOX/SNAPSHOT>> <NAME> [-- <ARGV>...]`

- `<NAME>`: Template name. A name in use gets a new build
- `--image <REF>`: An OCI image reference, such as `docker.io/library/python:3.12`
- `--dockerfile <FILE>`: A Dockerfile to build
- `--context <DIR>`: The build context directory for `--dockerfile`. Sent as a tar of at most 1 MiB. Empty when omitted
- `--build-arg <KEY=VALUE>`: A Dockerfile build argument, as key=value. Repeatable
- `--from-snapshot <SANDBOX/SNAPSHOT>`: A snapshot of one of your sandboxes, as SANDBOX/SNAPSHOT. No build runs
- `--registry-user <USER>`: The user name for a private registry
- `--registry-password-stdin`: Read the registry password or token from stdin
- `--tag <TAG>`: The tag to point at the build once it is ready. `default` when omitted
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`: The template description
- `--cpu <N>`: Virtual CPUs of a sandbox made from the build
- `--memory-mib <MIB>`: Memory in MiB of a sandbox made from the build
- `--disk-gib <GIB>`: Root filesystem in GiB of a sandbox made from the build
- `--env <KEY=VALUE>`: An environment variable of a sandbox made from the build, as key=value. Repeatable. Values are never shown again
- `--ready-port <PORT>`: The sandbox is running once this guest port takes a TCP connect
- `--ready-cmd <LINE>`: The sandbox is running once this shell line exits 0
- `--wait`: Wait until the build is ready or failed, then print it
- `--follow`: Print the build log on stderr until the build ends, then print the build
- `<ARGV>...`: The start command and its arguments, after `--`

## tritonctl sandbox template logs

Print the log of one build

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template logs [OPTIONS] <TEMPLATE> <BUILD>`

- `<TEMPLATE>`: Template name or uuid
- `<BUILD>`
- `--follow`: Keep printing until the build ends
- `--since <SEQ>`: Print only the lines after this one (default: 0)

## tritonctl sandbox template delete

Delete a template and every build of it

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template delete [OPTIONS] <TEMPLATE>`

- `<TEMPLATE>`: Template name or uuid
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails

## tritonctl sandbox template tag

Point a tag at a build

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template tag [OPTIONS] <TEMPLATE> <TAG> <BUILD>`

- `<TEMPLATE>`: Template name or uuid
- `<TAG>`
- `<BUILD>`

## tritonctl sandbox template untag

Remove a tag. The build stays

Usage: `tritonctl sandbox template untag [OPTIONS] <TEMPLATE> <TAG>`

- `<TEMPLATE>`: Template name or uuid
- `<TAG>`
